entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Vavrinec Dunajský (1784–1833) was a Slovak sculptor working in the Habsburg Kingdom of Hungary during the early nineteenth century. Active in a milieu of church commissions and town patronage, he produced religious statues and decorative sculpture that served Catholic parish life across Slovak-inhabited regions.

Dunajský’s career unfolded before the full romantic national revival yet within rising ethnic and linguistic self-awareness among Slovaks under Hungarian administration. Sacred sculpture remained a primary public art form, embedding local workshop talent in Baroque-to-neoclassical transitional styles.

He is remembered in Slovak art history as part of the craft lineage that sustained figurative sculpture in churches and squares prior to later monumental nationalism.
